1	# What waits on Alex: one page for one sitting (2026-11-16, D575)
     2	
     3	**In one line:** the new system is not ready to replace the running one.
     4	
     5	- The step that writes each question's answer choices still misses your quality gate.
     6	- The test of its final answers has not passed either.
     7	- Making it fit into the product has moved a long way.
     8	
     9	Six choices are yours, and nothing below decides them for you. Until you choose, the running system stays the default (D544).
    10	
    11	The two systems:
    12	
    13	- **The running system** is the pipeline that serves the product today.
    14	- **The new system** is the rebuilt pipeline (clean Steps 1 to 4). It reads news, opens questions, writes their answer choices and
    15	  judges them.
    16	
    17	## Your choices, in the order they were put to you
    18	
    19	### 1. Mark the pilot cards (Deck 1), about half an hour
    20	
    21	**What it is:** 19 cards from one stored week, with output from both systems; no card says which system wrote it.
    22	
    23	- 12 real answers and 2 planted wrong answers.
    24	- 2 matters no question took up.
    25	- 3 sheets of facts that never reached an answer.
    26	- 3 hidden repeats of earlier cards.
    27	
    28	**What you mark:**
    29	
    30	- On each answer card: is the question worth tracking (yes / no / cannot tell)? Is the answer supported by what is shown (yes / no /
    31	  cannot tell)?
    32	- On the two cards for matters no question took up: only whether the matter is worth tracking (there is no answer to mark).
    33	- On each fact sheet (its facts include one control that should not bear): does the fact bear on the question (yes / no / cannot
    34	  tell)? If it does, would it change the answer, only its confidence, neither, or cannot tell?
    35	- The deck's last box gives your marks as text to paste back; the counting needs the key held outside the repository.
    36	
    37	**Why it comes first:** since 2026-11-10 every judgement of quality has come from model readers, and their two families disagree. The
    38	deck tests whether your own reading can check them. It ranks neither system and passes no gate.
    39	
    40	**Where:** [`pilot-deck-1/deck-1.html`](pilot-deck-1/deck-1.html), opened in a browser.
    41	
    42	### 2. What role should your six lines play for the answer-choice step?
    43	
    44	**Your six lines (D400):**
    45	
    46	1. No set of answer choices asks a different question from its topic.
    47	2. None leaves a part of its topic unlisted.
    48	3. None has an outcome with no matching answer, or with two.
    49	4. No refusal without a justified reason.
    50	5. At least 35 of the 44 topics right in at least two of three attempts, at least 28 of them with written answer choices.
    51	6. The same favourable direction in all three attempts for every company figure, and the same due day for at least nine in ten topics.
    52	
    53	(The later readings had fewer topics than 44; the council scaled line 5 to them as a diagnostic, not as your line.)
    54	
    55	**The record:** the gate has been missed in all nine readings. Not every line failed each time: in the latest reading line 4 was met,
    56	and line 6 could not be measured there (too few topics of the kinds it covers).
    57	
    58	**New (D568, D569):** we read the same 39 answer choices again with fresh readers of the same two model families.
    59	
    60	- Every line came out the same as before.
    61	- The same seven attempts failed line 2.
    62	
    63	That is repeatability under one method. It is not proof that each mark is right.
    64	
    65	**Also new:**
    66	
    67	- **Line 2's field had no reader.** The parts a question leaves unjudged were shown nowhere until today; they now appear beside each
    68	  answer.
    69	- **One reading mark checks a field still unread.** It is not one of your six lines but a mark the readers give (an event's stated plan,
    70	  part of the reference); that field is read nowhere in the product.
    71	- **A paper recount:** with both of those marks set aside (the unjudged-parts mark and the event-reference mark), 9 or 7 of 13 topics
    72	  come out right, against 11 needed. The recount was not done with only the reference mark set aside.
    73	
    74	**Options:**
    75	
    76	- Keep all six lines, read with every mark, as the gate.
    77	- Decide separately what role each disputed mark should play (the unjudged-parts mark, now shown on the page; the event-reference
    78	  mark, read nowhere).
    79	- Set new lines after your Deck 1 reading.
    80	
    81	**Until you choose:** the gate stays as written and stays unmet.
    82	
    83	### 3. What should the next product test start from? (D559)
    84	
    85	**The choice:**
    86	
    87	- **Option A:** confirm that the next product-oriented test starts from a real library of questions already held, built by an earlier
    88	  run. Tests that start from empty can stay as diagnostics.
    89	- **Option B:** choose another starting condition.
    90	
    91	**Evidence, with its limits (D561 to D564):**
    92	
    93	- **Small comparison, 11 articles:** read once from a held library and once from empty. The held library opened 4 new questions where
    94	  the empty start opened 16. It did not open a separate equity-commitments question that the empty start opened; those facts went under
    95	  a held question, and both reader families accepted that home. By the rule written before the run, the result fell between its two
    96	  outcomes.
    97	- **The fortnight run, one draw:** week 2's six new questions repeated none of the held ones. This cannot show the problem is solved in
    98	  general.
    99	
   100	**Until you choose:** each test states its own starting condition.
   101	
   102	### 4. Answers placed with nothing behind them (D520)
   103	
   104	**The problem has two cases, which need not get the same answer:**
   105	
   106	- **Case one:** nothing shown to the judge sizes the amount, yet it names a band.
   107	- **Case two:** the estimate rests on an unsupported step the judge supplied itself (a discount, a growth rate), and that step decides
   108	  the band. (A step the judge supplies is not wrong in itself; the case is the unsupported one.)
   109	
   110	**Options for each case:**
   111	
   112	- Show the band as today.
   113	- Show it with a plain label of what it rests on.
   114	- Show no band.
   115	
   116	No recommendation is recorded among these.
   117	
   118	**What was tried (D565, D566):**
   119	
   120	- **Asking the judge:** asked after the fact which band its own evidence sized, the judge did not separate the answers readers had
   121	  failed from those they had passed.
   122	- **Two reader families:** they mostly agreed on the narrower mark that no amount was the answer's starting point, and split on
   123	  whether a scaled comparable is a basis. That narrower observation came after the fact, and the check's own verdict was "unclear".
   124	
   125	Neither a label nor a "no band" rule has been built or tested.
   126	
   127	**Until you choose:** the band is shown, as today.
   128	
   129	### 5. Two directions the running product invents (D571); two separate choices
   130	
   131	**5a. Yes/No questions:** "Yes" is coloured as good news and "No" as bad. A "Yes" can be bad for the company. Change it, or keep it.
   132	
   133	**5b. Theme ranges:** the highest range is scored +2 by inference. For a theme such as memory prices, higher may be bad. Change it,
   134	or keep it.
   135	
   136	**What the new system does instead:**
   137	
   138	- Its events, and its theme ranges with no registered favourable direction, are shown in neutral colours, with no score.
   139	- An Idea's combined score is not computed when one of these is among its drivers, and the Idea card says which one.
   140	
   141	### 6. Running the new system live
   142	
   143	**Three separate things are open:**
   144	
   145	1. **Resuming the design.** It is paused (D575): a live database needs an operating contract (its side files, long reads, dates not
   146	   yet complete, every reader that opens it).
   147	2. **How live data is read.** Today's working rule never opens a live run's database directly, only a snapshot (AGENTS §9). A live
   148	   service could keep that rule and serve copies, or relax it.
   149	3. **When to adopt.** Adopting the new system at all comes after the quality gates.
   150	
   151	**Two known gaps:**
   152	
   153	- **First day (open defect 10):** on a new database's very first day, before that day completes, the service would show the day
   154	  half-done.
   155	- **A failed live read is silent:** if the page cannot reach the service, it quietly keeps the copy built into the page. This is as
   156	  specified today. A small "collected snapshot" note is a possible change, for your choice.
   157	
   158	**Meanwhile:** the design is paused by the council (D575), which may resume it under D439; the read rule and the silent fallback stay
   159	as they are until you choose.
   160	
   161	## What is in force meanwhile
   162	
   163	- **The product:** the running system serves it, unchanged.
   164	- **The council:** works under D439, deciding reversibly and recording each decision. Any paid send needs its own decision, within the
   165	  $40 ceiling; about $26.07 is used.
   166	- **The new system's integration, checked on stored replays and serving tests:**
   167	  - the page shows its questions, including the parts each question does not judge, with no invented direction;
   168	  - due questions close on their due day, as in the running system;
   169	  - a freshly opened page shows the latest completed day.
   170	  - Still open: the first-day defect, the live-service design and the Idea planner on a new-system database.
   171	- **Next, at no cost:** a count of whether the judge test (Stage B) can reach the eight comparison questions it needs *within its
   172	  fixed set* (D575). No paid run follows without its own decision.
   173	
   174	## Where the evidence is
   175	
   176	- **The record of this stretch:** decisions D559 to D575 (`docs/DECISIONS-log.md`).
   177	- **The round log:** §§53 to 57 (`LEAN-LOG.md`).
   178	- **The page and serving checks:** `page-contract/` (`RESULT.md`, `SERVE-RESULT.md`, `SERVING-WHILE-WRITING-RESULT.md`).
   179	- **The repeated reading:** `gate1-stick/RESULT.md`.
   180	- **The fortnight run:** `carried-run/RESULT.md`.
   181	- **The earlier page:** `DECISION-PAGE-2026-11-15.md`.
